subject: chemistry
title: Partition coefficient
key_idea: The partition coefficient, Kpc, is the ratio of the concentrations of a solute in two immiscible solvents at equilibrium. It depends on the polarity of the solute and of each solvent.

blocks.text: A solute shaken with two solvents that do not mix will distribute itself between them. The ratio of its concentrations settles at a constant value.

items.meaning: The ratio of the concentrations of a solute in two immiscible solvents, at equilibrium, at a given temperature.
Describes liquids that do not mix, such as water and hexane.

blocks.label: Partition coefficient
where: Kpc = partition coefficient (no unit if the concentration units match)
[X] = concentration of the solute at equilibrium (mol/dm³ or g/dm³)

items: The ratio is constant at a constant temperature.
The solute must be in the same physical state, and the same molecular form, in both solvents. It must not associate or dissociate in one of them.
State which solvent is on top of the fraction. Kpc for solvent 2 ÷ solvent 1 is the reciprocal.
Kpc is a ratio of concentrations in two immiscible solvents.
It applies when the solute is in the same state in both.

blocks.text: Use the expression to find a concentration, or to find how much solute ends up in each layer.

items.text: Let the mass in one solvent be m, so the other holds the total minus m.
Divide each mass by the volume of its solvent.
Put the concentrations into Kpc and solve for m.

blocks.text: X has Kpc = 8.0 for ether ÷ water. 1.0 g of X in 100 cm³ water is shaken with 50 cm³ ether. Then 2m ÷ (1.0 − m) = 8.0, so m = 0.80 g is in the ether.

diagram.alt: A practice question using a partition coefficient to find a concentration.
diagram.question: A solute has Kpc = {k} (ether ÷ water). Its concentration in the water layer is {w} g/dm³. Calculate its concentration in the ether layer.

items: Several small extractions remove more solute than one large one of the same total volume.
In the example, two extractions with 25 cm³ of ether remove 0.89 g, compared with 0.80 g from one 50 cm³ extraction.
Kpc = concentration in solvent 1 ÷ concentration in solvent 2.
Repeated extractions with small portions are more effective.

blocks.text: Kpc is large when the solute is much more soluble in one solvent. This depends on polarity.

items: A polar or ionic solute dissolves better in a polar solvent such as water. It can form hydrogen bonds or ion-dipole attractions with water.
A non-polar solute dissolves better in a non-polar solvent such as hexane. It forms instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces.
Kpc is therefore large for a solute whose polarity matches one solvent and not the other.
Temperature also changes Kpc, so it is quoted at a stated temperature.

rows: Non-polar, so it is not attracted to polar water
Ionic, so it forms ion-dipole attractions with water
Its many OH groups hydrogen bond to water

items: Polar solutes prefer polar solvents. Non-polar solutes prefer non-polar solvents.

checks.q: State what is meant by the partition coefficient of a solute between two solvents.
checks.a: The ratio of the concentration of the solute in one solvent to its concentration in the other solvent, at equilibrium and constant temperature (the two solvents being immiscible).

checks.q: Kpc for a compound between ether and water is 12 (ether ÷ water). The concentration in water is 0.050 mol/dm³. Calculate its concentration in ether.
Suggest why iodine has a large Kpc for hexane ÷ water.
checks.a: Iodine is non-polar. It dissolves well in non-polar hexane through instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces and poorly in polar water.
